#4137. GTA 6: Best Ways to Make Money

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Money makes the world go round, and that certainly is the case for Grand Theft Auto 6. This is one of, if not the biggest game to ever be released, and in order to make it big in the massive world Rockstar has established, you need to take on some jobs. Some are shady while others are slightly less shady.

Most require some sort of crime, but for the most part, it’s not too difficult to earn millions by the end of the adventure. This guide will help you make money from the early stages of the game to the late stages. For example, the first two chapters only has a couple of ways to make money, while the end game has a slew of options, but only one that’s worth it.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

For the first chapter, it’s primarily doing side activities such as Kenton’s scuba treasure dives or ripping off the Kingfishers gangs. Both pay decently for early game adventures and encounters.

By far the best way to make money in the second chapter, and really throughout the entire game, is stealing cars and selling them. Early in the game, you’ll only have access to some cheaper vehicles, so look out for any type of van that might be hauling some items, such as a news van. These will generally net you above $1,000. It’s a start.

When you get to Vice City, you will meet a man named Randy who wants some very nice cars, and in order to do this, you will need to obtain the ability to clone a key. Thankfully, he shows you, and you can earn a lot of money with him. The downside is that the higher the price on the car, the more likely it’ll have an Advanced Tracker, which is a pain to deal with. It’s almost better to go with mid-payout vehicles with Standard Trackers and drive carefully, which will net you a condition bonus.

This is technically good in the early stages of the game, but when you get halfway through the campaign, you’ll likely have access to more hardware, faster getaway vehicles and body armor. At this point, you’ll have some cash put aside to get the job done easier, so take advantage of this.

Another means of getting paid is ripping off gangs. There will be various set-ups all throughout Vice City and the northern region with a decent pay day. They will also have key valuables that can be sold for quite a bit, on top of unique weapons and cars that you might want to add to your personal collection.

When you get into the five couple of chapters, there will be some very good opportunities to make some real money. As you learn through the campaign, you need more and more money, and bank robberies are the endgame ways to make money. This is because, while you can take on small banks for upwards of $20,000, some of the big banks can make upwards of ten times that.

The problem is that these are very difficult to overcome. You will need to ensure everyone stays in line and no bank alarms go off too early. Then there’s getting away from the cops, which can be challenging. But if you’re able to do it, the pay is worth it.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4136. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

#4135. MTG Star Trek Card Featuring Patrick Stewart Sells At $26K

Magic: The Gathering isn't exactly a stranger when it comes to ridiculously expensive cards, and while resellers aren't quite as rabid as some other TCGs, even somewhat less popular sets like Star Trek are still reaching hefty prices on the second-hand market. While the price might not compete with Lord of the Rings' over $2M One Ring card, getting one of MTG's new serialized cards will still cost you quite a bit.

While the seven hand-signed card variants introduced in MTG's Star Trek Collector's Boosters were already going to be a massive hit due to their limited availability, one of them has already broken the $20,000 mark, albeit for a bit of a morbid reason.

As shared by moombahh on Reddit, while most autographed Star Trek cards go for around $5-10K USD, a recent eBay listing for none other than Captain Jean-Luc Picard reportedly sold for a whopping $26K. While it's entirely possible the buyer sent a lower offer, it might even end up on the cheaper side of the spectrum if the other eBay listings are anything to go by.

With more recent listings having shot up all the way to $38K and an even more massive $45K, the price could wind up being well above the last sold price, and it's not hard to see why either.

For the first time ever, you can pack signed MTG cards, with seven to collect in total, but the first two revealed are of Captains Kirk and Janeway.

Dwarfing the Secret Lair card prices, the main reason players have been pricing their cards so high is that, since signing the cards, Jean-Luc Picard's actor, Patrick Stewart, recently passed away, leaving the serialized cards among the last items signed by the legendary actor.

While fans have pointed out that it's more than a little depressing that others are trying to capitalize on the late actor's passing by selling the cards for absurd prices, it's unlikely that sellers will be slowing down anytime soon, considering how limited their availability will continue to be.

"Grand Theft Auto VI, the most preordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store, launches November 19," an Xbox blog post reads. "Considering the unprecedented demand, we encourage everyone to begin preloading as soon as possible to ensure you're prepared for launch day." PlayStation echoes this statement with a blog post of its own that reads, "Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most preordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store. The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

Catch up on the latest set of Genshin Impact codes before you play, and check out why we think Genshin Impact is one of the best mobile games you can play today.

#4131. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

#4130. GTA 6: How to Unlock the Ultimate Edition Content

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

For those who decided to dish out the extra cash to buy the Ultimate Edition of Grand Theft Auto 6, then you’ll get quite a bit for your dollar. The Ultimate Edition comes with a slew of in-game items, but most of them aren’t unlocked immediately.

While some will appear on Jason’s property right away, most are tied to shops within the game or are found after certain events further into the story, some of which are only available basically at the end. With that said, this will hopefully give you a good idea where to find everything.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

These are the first two vehicles you’ll have access to outside of Jason’s Ganado muscle car after you start the game. They will be conveniently placed near Jason’s house in Chapter 1 to take for a ride.

The Ganado Retro Build is one of the first Ultimate Edition item you can get in your campaign, and it’s the easiest. All you will need to do, starting in Chapter 1, is drive into a Pay ‘N’ Spray with Jason’s Ganado, which will be impounded past Chapter 2, and go into Complete Kits. The first option should be the Retro Build, which upgrades Jason’s wheels decently, at least for a starter vehicle.

There are a couple of revolvers ready to be picked up at an Ammu-Nation locker whenever Lucia gains access to them starting in Chapter 2. These are powerful guns that should be put in your arsenal.

On top of that, there are weapon variants for a handful of guns, such as the Girardi ES9 and Klose K17, which can be customized at a locker whenever you see fit. These will upgrade the two weapons nicely.

This is technically available at the beginning of the game, but you likely won’t come up to the shopping district that houses this store until Chapter 3. This is located within Vice City’s southern portion of the map and has some rather nice new clothes for you to pick up. The downside is that you have to bye them in-game.

Hair is an important feature, so why not hit up Sara’s Unisex Salon? The signature hair is found at every salon in the game, but the unique hairstyles are located in Hamlet starting in Chapter 1. This is located relatively close to the correctional facility.

This is the first boat you’ll be able to own, but it’s only available in Chapter 4. As soon as you move into your new apartment and kick off the chapter, there will be a new icon immediately to the northwest. You’ll find the boat here at the Washington Bach canal dock.

One of the most iconic cars in GTA Vice City, you’re able to pick up this vehicle much later in the game, specifically in Chapter 5 at the Pegassi Residences.

#4129. Top War tier list - Every hero ranked

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 1.685.0

In Top War, there are quite a lot of things that you could consider 'farmable', and in certain situations, heroes might be considered one of these things. And since there are just so many heroes out there, it could be quite difficult to choose a handful and make them your number one priority.

Don't despair though, below we've compiled a Top War tier list of all the best heroes in the game so you can choose the best ones according to your needs. The heroes can provide specific buffs and their kit can be extremely good in certain situations, but if you really want some additional info about these heroes, I've got you covered.

Most of the heroes on the Top War tier list are SSR Before we take a look at the Top War tier list though, I'll start by mentioning that the rarity of the heroes (SSR, SR, and R) plays a very important role in the game. The higher a hero's rarity, the more troops can join them in battle (SSR heroes can take a lot more troops than R heroes).

Therefore, it shouldn't come as a surprise that all the top-tier heroes are SSR. If you want to get SSR heroes too, all you need to do is keep playing the game - even as a f2p player you are bound to get a few eventually!

All the heroes have a type - some of them are Air Force heroes, some are Army heroes, and others are Navy Heroes. In the tier list, you will find them all divided by their type, so it will be a lot easier for you to pick the best ones based on what they should specialize in.

If you want to learn more about the game, make sure you check out our other Top War articles!

Maximo - A powerful hero that will greatly enhance any air force units and can quite literally change the entire course of a battle. He's a premium hero who is worth investing in, and by all means, one who can work on the offensive and defensive front.

Selina - She's a good hero thanks to the amazing buffs she provides, and if you manage to max her out, she greatly increases the maximum HP of other units, as well as their attack. Serval - Another broken premium hero that can make life a living hell for enemies. She's especially good when paired up with some of the other top-tier heroes, since they can stack their stats.

Preycis - This Army hero is great for aiming at the back-row enemies and is one of the best at specialising in that. He doesn't have a whole lot of other buffs (when compared to other heroes), but the sheer amount of damage dealt to the back row cannot go unnoticed. Shinji Ikari - A highly versatile hero, he can be obtained for a limited time only, but during that time, it's crucial to get him. He can be used for pretty much any type of content and has an ability that grants indestructibility for two rounds, which is definitely worth it. Optimus Prime - Another collab character that is impossible to overlook is Optimus Prime, the best Transformer out there (correct?). He can also grant an indestructibility buff, and when maxed out, is absolutely top-tier.

#4128. Nioh 3 is, unsurprisingly, the fastest-selling game in the series with over a million units sold

Nioh 3 has taken the Nioh franchise to new heights, delivering its biggest-ever launch.

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”

#4127. The fastest cars in CSR Racing 2, in every tier

Updated with the very best cars to race in 2026

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 6.7.2

Want to quickly compare stats on all the cars in CSR Racing 2? Then this is the guide for you.

Below, we've listed all the base stats for every car and highlighted which wins in each category. R stands for Rep Bonus, and F is for Fusion Slots.

Obviously, every car can be completely changed through upgrades and tuning, but these starting numbers give you a good indication of that car's overall abilities. It provides a quick glimpse at the stats, which might just be enough to help you pick out which car to choose to purchase next.

We've also included some thoughts on which are the best cars in CSR Racing 2 - both rare imports and those you can buy with in-game cash.

Just click through below to find out the fastest cars in every tier.

Many great choices in this category. At first glance, it seems like the Golf GTI MK1 is a clear winner, especially as it also has a 6% RP bonus and eight fusion slots. However, it must be won in the Rare Imports lot, which means it's a lot harder to come by.

On top of that, the fastest car so far is the Ford Mustang Boss 302 with e.c level 50, which means, even though it's not as fast early on, it can make it up in the later stages.

The Veloster Turbo R Spec is also a decent choice, but can only be purchased with (150) Gold.

The M235i Coupe is a fantastic car for Tier 2, especially since you can buy it for just $75,000. It's light and has high power, but you'll need to upgrade your tyres to bring the grip up.

Potentially, the Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Coupe can be the fastest in this tier and by quite a big margin. Not early on, though. The same goes for the Ferrari 250 GTO and Aston Martin DB5.

If you want Tier 2's best vehicle, you'll need to earn the F-150 from the Rare Imports lot.

The Ferrari California 30 is obviously still one of the best Tier 3 cars in class - no wonder it's being kept back as a prize.

So if you can't win that, the SRT Hellcat at 825 G is a good choice with its high power, low shift time, and strong grip. If you only have dollars to spend, get the RS 5 Coupe.

At level 50, the Pontiac GTO "The Judge" is the fastest car in this category. The BMW M2 (G87) Coupe "M Performance" is right behind it in second place. As you would expect, any variant of the Civic Type R is going to be fast! This is one of my favourite categories, as there are several good choices.

The GT-R (R35) Premium looks like a pretty good vehicle for this tier. Not only is it affordable, but it has an amazing grip (too much, perhaps?!) and a low shift time. You'll need to work on power and lowering the weight with a lighter body.

The Viper ACR is another good option: it has great power for the tier, a low shift time, and 23 Fusion Slots.

Right now, the Rocket Bunny is looking more attractive than ever, but the big Grand Cherokee Trackhawk is tempting too.

At this point, the game has some amazing cars to use, and the latest releases push performance to the limits. These are by far the fastest cars in CSR Racing 2. The Bugatti Chiron is a fantastic choice, as is the FXX K, but launch cars such as the Bugatti Veyron and One:1 are still great.

If you don't want to rely on Rare Import lot wins, the Aventador LP 700-4 is a good bet with its high power, strong grip, and its relatively lightweight to boot.

Regardless, though, there's no doubt you'll have fun with vehicles like the 'Cuda "TorC" in CSR2.

#4126. Where To Play Every Game Of The Year Nominee For 2026

The votes have been cast and the nominees for 2026's Game of the Year have been revealed. Six of the past year's biggest and best games, and as always, the games that have and haven't made the cut are being hotly debated. There's also a remake in the mix this year along with a game that hadn't been released when the nominations were announced, so a lot for those who think the awards should have clearer criteria to discuss.

Whether you agree with all six nominees or not, it's hard to argue that the games in the running this year aren't six of the six biggest games released this calendar year. The games that, if you haven't played anything else this year, or if there are some you missed, you should probably try your best to play before we get to 2027 and another year of new games begins. Whether you're wondering whether you have the right hardware before buying the nominees, want to know if they have a physical release, or you just want to know how much they cost, you'll find everything you need to know to fill in your GOTY gaps below.

GTA 6 is finally here, and its Game of the Year nomination has caused a stir. The game will be here by the time the awards are handed out, but it was nominated two days before release. That doesn't matter to you right now, though. The launch of GTA 6 is mere hours away as I type this, and if you're not one of the 15 million people who have placed a pre-order, here's what you need to know.

As long as you ignore the state of rent, wages, and world economics, GTA 6's price tag isn't that bad, you guys!

GTA 6 will only be available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S when released. Its PC launch will follow at a later, still unrevealed, time. There are two editions to choose from - standard and ultimate. The standard edition will provide tens, if not hundreds, of hours of entertainment, but there will be various stores, barbers, and tattoo parlors that are off-limits if you don't own the ultimate edition.

The standard edition of GTA 6 is $79.99 on both PS5 and Series X|S, while the ultimate edition is $99.99 on both platforms.

GTA 6 isn't the only game that has caused a stir by picking up a GOTY nomination this year. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has poked the beehive that is remakes being eligible to win the prestigious award. If there was ever a remake that was going to qualify, it's a universally loved one like this that somehow reimagines one of the greatest games of all time without upsetting any of the original's fans.

There is only one place you can play the Ocarina of Time remake, and that's on Switch 2. There are no different editions to choose from, but there is a physical release, and since this is a Switch 2 exclusive, there's a price difference between its digital and physical versions. A digital copy of Ocarina of Time costs $59.99, but if you want a physical copy, it'll cost you $69.99.

Robert Pattinson might be the next James Bond on the big screen, but Patrick Gibson became the video game Bond this year in the critically acclaimed 007 First Light. A performance so good that not only were fans suggesting Gibson could potentially make the jump to Bond movies, but the odds of that happening spiked significantly after the game was released.

First Light is the first nominee on the list that's available to play on Steam. It's also on PS5 and Series X|S, and while a Switch 2 version was promised, it has been delayed until March 18, 2027. I have played a little bit of the game on Switch 2, and for what it's worth, I didn't encounter any issues and was a little surprised that its release was moved into 2027.

It's amazing to see just how far this series has come since the low point that was Resident Evil 6. The trilogy that has followed, alongside the remakes of games from its heyday, has put Resident Evil firmly back on top of the video game mountain. That's why Resident Evil Requiem, a game many would describe as the best new Resi game in decades, is in the running to be crowned Game of the Year.

If you're trying to play all of these games before a winner is crowned, or you want to get one under your belt quickly, Requiem is the place to start. By far the shortest nominee on this year's GOTY list, with a story that takes around 11 hours to play through according to How Long To Beat. It's also the only one of all six nominees that's available on all major platforms, with those who played on Switch 2 awarding it, and Capcom's other day-one Switch 2 releases this year, high praise.

Phantom Blade Zero is a game people have been waiting a long time for. Shown off for the first time well over three years ago, S-Game's action-packed epic finally arrived in October, and it did not disappoint. Rave reviews and a player base that wholeheartedly agrees with what the critics had to say about it have landed it among 2026's Game of the Year nominees.

Your platform options are limited for this one - just PS5 for console players, but it is on PC too if you prefer to play there. There's no physical release either, which is unfortunate, although a physical edition of the PS5 version has been promised for 2027. Hopefully there aren't any issues getting that out on time, with PlayStation pushing forward with its promise to stop putting games on discs in 2028.

Control Resonant might be the most surprising inclusion among this year's Game of the Year nominees. Not because it doesn't deserve to be on this list, but because it's the only game of the six where the combined reaction to its release wasn't overwhelmingly positive, unlike the other five. Not that many people had anything negative to say about it, just that it didn't seem to blow everyone away quite as much as its GOTY competitors.

Now that said, if you want to play the best games 2026 has to offer, Control Resonant should unquestionably be on your list, particularly if you liked the first game and you're an Alan Wake fan. It's available on PS5, Xbox, and PC, there's a physical version if you're into that kind of thing, and it's slightly more expensive and includes an extra outfit, resources, and a digital artbook and soundtrack.

Steam has incredible sales all year round, but nothing quite compares to the deals you can get during the holiday season!

#4125. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#4124. Thrifty Business review - "The coziest management sim you'll ever play"

I never thought I'd come across something that manages to impress me to this extent - until Thrifty Business, at least. And let me tell you: I was beyond impressed. So, this is not just a simple Thrifty Business review; this is me telling you why you need to give it a try.

I play a lot of games. And by a lot, I mean A LOT. So, at this point, it takes quite a bit for something to genuinely surprise me.

I expected a cute little shop management sim (as per the Play Store images). Maybe something to play for a few hours and decorate a few shelves. Well, it didn't happen quite like that. I ended up spending far more time than I'd expected rearranging furniture and getting excited over witchy items.

In essence, you can buy unwanted items from NPCs in the form of mystery boxes. Then, you place them on the shelves and organise them by category. Later on, you can even organise events and expand. That's it.

Honestly, what's not to love? Grab your tea and blanket and get cosy - we'll talk gameplay! In terms of gameplay, you have all the freedom you need as a shopkeeper. You can genuinely make the place feel like your own. From finding the perfect spot for an item to rearranging displays, you're the boss.

You can even redecorate as much as you like - there's no restriction on that (thankfully), so in a way, you can play this in your own way. I mean, you can even skip decorating altogether and just play for the dialogue or for making money.

Personally, I'm always going to choose decorating over anything else, even at the cost of buying additional items.

On the topic of additional items, Thrifty Business doesn't try to turn running a shop into a stressful experience. There's no pressure to maximise every penny or deal with impatient customers.

Even if you end up making no sales in a day, the system still has a way to keep you progressing by offering a free mystery box every day. Not that they're particularly expensive (at the beginning, at least), but it's little details like this that make me appreciate the thought put into the experience.

Just a fair warning though: it's the kind of sim where you tell yourself "I'll play for another ten minutes", only to realise an entire hour flew by. The pixel graphics: love at first sight Can we please talk about the aesthetics?

The colourful 90s atmosphere makes the entire experience feel like a warm hug.

As someone who grew up during that time, seeing all those nostalgic items brought into 2026 put a smile on my face. I'd almost forgotten all about the Slinky!

Since I mentioned it, let me make one thing clear: there are a lot of items you can acquire in Thrifty Business. I mean A LOT. With so many of them, it's hard not to appreciate the sheer amount of work that must have gone into designing all those individual sprites. Not everyone's cup of tea - but maybe everyone's cup of hot cocoa? I have to admit, Thrifty Business understands exactly what kind of experience it wants to offer. It's not one of those fast-paced tycoons where you rush to make millions from the get-go.

That might not make it into everyone's favourite list, but it is bound to make it into some. If you're over here reading this and you have someone special in your life who likes Stardew Valley, then Thrifty Business is something you can definitely surprise them with.

Really, sometimes, all you need is to escape into a cute little world, put things on shelves, decorate to your heart's content, and call it a day. Life is too fast-paced sometimes anyway, and Thrifty Business can be the escape that is one tap away. You need to play with the sound on The audio deserves some love too, and I believe Spellgarden Games did an amazing job creating a soundtrack that perfectly complements the sim. I honestly couldn't fault it at all, and I'm usually the type to turn the sound off after spending more than five hours with a game. Not this time, though...

An ode to the queer community As if the cosy atmosphere wasn't enough, I absolutely adore the queer representation woven into this.

From the story (which you should absolutely read - I won't give you any spoilers) to the item categories and even character creation, there's something about the sense of community you get in this little virtual world that gives you a fuzzy feeling inside. Not too many games celebrate individuality, self-expression, and simply being yourself in a way that feels "just right".

Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a shop to rearrange. Again.

#4123. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4122. GTA 6: How to Get into Bank Vaults

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most complex and grandiose open worlds there has ever been, and because of its name, there will be a bit of stealth. But it’s not cars you’re stealing, or at least not in this guide. Here, we are talking about Lucia and Jason finding their way into a higher payday, and to do that, they will need to rob some more advanced locations, specifically banks. With this guide, you’ll learn how to get into the vault, where all the money is kept.

So, you’re fed up with the cash from the drawers in banks and the small safes in the back rooms and want some of the bigger dough. Well, there’s only one way to do that: through the bank vaults.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

Getting into a bank vault isn’t easy as it requires a lot of planning and work. Well, a little bit. Unfortunately, the first requirement in order to get into a bank vault will likely be disappointing to most people: you need to be at the end of Chapter 4. This means that you have done jobs for Yasmani in Vice City and have completed the VCIA Takedown mission, one of the biggest heists in the game.

After completing this, you will be given some time to cooldown and lie low. But for Jason and Lucia, that means finding more creative ways of robbing. Yasmani will contact you about a money truck coming around Little Cuba. Head to the Cuban Restaurant, Café Orquidea and wait. This will unlock the That’s Where the Money Is … quest.

Here you will have to tail a money truck, don't get too close until it reaches its destination: Lombank – Ocean Beach. This is one of the smaller banks in the area, having only medium security but a decent amount of take if you’re up to the challenge. Once both you and the money truck have parked, head inside and stick the place up. Head through the back door and rob the vault as it’s open thanks to the money truck making a pickup (or dropoff).

The challenging part is, because you robbed the vault, you now have four stars, which can be trouble to get away from. Thankfully, there is a dock nearby, and taking a high-speed boat out into the open waters has a greater chance of escape. Once you do, unfortunately, the island is now looking for you.

Thankfully, now that you have gotten your first taste of the vault, you’ll want more. Thankfully, Yasmani will now offer tips for when a security van is making a pickup or drop off, allowing you to time when to go shopping.

After that, all you need to do is call or visit Yasmani and you can take one of the money vaults in Vice City. Mind you, it will cost you $10,000 for the tip, but the take will be much larger. Just be prepared for some heavy gunfire.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4121. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

#4120. Vampire Survivors tier list - Ranking characters from base game and DLCs

Each DLC brought different characters and we have decided to rank each one and rank them on the Vampire Survivors tier list according to their late-game power.

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 1.16.111

Since the release of Vampire Survivors, people have been widely discussing things like "Who are the best characters in the game?" and other burning questions. There are, god knows, how many characters at the moment, but even then, this list can still expand with every update. Picking the most powerful character is essential to enjoying Vampire Survivors, and we are here to help with that.

Potent characters will mean an easier time, so if you're not looking for a challenge, they're the way to go. If you're playing with any of them, you can kill enemies much more effectively and win even if you are a beginner. Below are the best characters in Vampire Survivors. Also, feel free to check our Dead Cells weapons tier list as well as this tier list for Capybara Go.

About Queen Sigma Even though Queen Sigma can't pick up Golden Eggs like other heroes, she is still one of the most powerful characters, and it wouldn't be wrong to call her the best character without a doubt.

She uses the Victory Sword, which is one of the game’s most potent weapons. After levelling up, she gets +1% Might and +1% Growth, allowing her to become much more powerful. The main feature of Queen Sigma is her 333 max health, allowing her to survive longer.

About Red Death Red Death is the fastest and scariest hero in Vampire Survivors. The high speed makes this character suitable for finding Relic locations and fighting hidden bosses. Red Death uses the Death Spiral that can be easily combined with Axe in the same run. Its main feature is the 20% Might increase and the 100% Movement increase. These stats make Red Death one of the most potent heroes in Vampire Survivors.

Pungola is a mighty Vampire Survivors character that has two primary weapons: Phiera Der Tuphello and Eight The Sparrow. The hero gets +1% Might every level and can be unlocked by opening a special coffin in Mad Forest. Also, you should cast the spell “flymetothemoon” in Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane to unlock this hero.

Ambrojoe is an easily attainable hero that uses La Robba as a primary weapon. This character has average stats and no special abilities, making him the best option for beginners. We have to note that the weapon looks an awful lot like a Kinder Egg - we're actually not sure if it's an easter egg or not.

Dommario can be a good option for beginners due to his powerful defence and attack stats, but the main disadvantage of Dommario is speed. It is one of the slowest characters you can choose.

Megalo Menya Moonspell is overall the best character in Legacy of Moonspell DLC due to her combination of survivability and damage.

What stands out particularly is her invincibility, meaning she cannot take damage at all during certain periods. That said, this comes with a limitation; she will disappear when the current time limit expires. This makes her particularly powerful for clearing stages quickly.

Je-Ne-Viv is considered the most powerful character in Tides of the Foscari DLC, and that's why she's at the top of this part of our Vampire Survivors tier list. She has a unique weapon called Insatiable, which scales with Magnet and Greed stats, and comes with the Shadow Servant. Her abilities deal significant area-of-effect damage, making her a powerful character overall.

Crewmate Dino gains permanent stat boosts whenever any player's weapon reaches its max level. This ability makes him especially powerful in co-op mode, making him the best character in the Emergency Meeting DLC.

Megalo Impostor Rina has high base stats, special weapon mechanics, and the ability to scale through all phases of the game. Her toolkit is ideal for those who enjoy a playstyle that rewards aggressive tactics and strategic planning.

About Colonel Bahamut Colonel Bahamut stands out because of his great passive bonuses, like +100 Max Health and +50% Might. His weapon, Metal Claw, allows for significant area damage, making him the best character in Operation Guns DLC, capable of scaling effectively with Greed and Curse mechanics.

About Alucard Alucard is S-Tier and one of the best characters in the Ode to Castlevania DLC due to his high damage output, versatility, and healing abilities. His weapon mechanics allow for powerful area control, making him a top-tier choice for most runs.

Sonia Belmont is the other top-tier character in Ode to Castlevania. She has excellent scaling potential and powerful weapon synergies. Her ability to deal consistent dps while maintaining survivability is what makes her so good.

About Vlad Tepes Dracula Vlad Tepes Dracula has a deserving top position on this Vampire Survivors tier list since he is a character with high damage output and abilities that enhance survivability. His skills allow him to deal significant area damage, making him a standout choice for many players.

About Lisa Tepes Lisa Tepes provides excellent support with healing abilities and buffs that can sustain her and allies throughout runs. Her versatility and ability to boost stats make her invaluable in longer gameplay sessions. About Cornell Cornell has strong offensive capabilities with transformation mechanics that allow him to adapt to different combat scenarios effectively. His versatility makes him a solid choice for various builds.

About Cosmo Even though Cosmo looks cute, he is one of the deadliest heroes in Vampire Survivors. The main feature of this character is that he does not have a primary weapon. So, you have more customisation options using Cosmo compared to other heroes. About Leda The primary weapon for Leda is the Holy Land, the improved version of the Magic Wand. She can equip both weapons to reach the highest effectiveness in the same run. Leda also has Passive Bonuses, which you can find below:

Gyorunton is another dragon in Tier S. It uses the Bracelet to kill enemies and has a special ability - Gyorunton can evolve weapons much faster than other heroes using Treasure Chest. Also, this hero has 300 Max Health, which is exceptionally high compared to the classic 100 Health Points.

About Smith IV Smith IV is a scary character who uses Vandalier as a primary weapon. This hero has +100% Luck and gets +1% Luck at every level, which is a unique ability. And for such a decisive boost, Smith IV pays with his stats.

About Gain Boros Gains Boros is a mighty dragon that uses Heaven Sword as the primary weapon. This character gains +2% Growth every time you level it up, making Heaven Sword more powerful.

And that’s our complete Vampire Survivors tier list. As you can see, the game has a significant diversity of exciting characters, and 3 of the best heroes in Vampire Survivors are Queen Sigma, Red Death, and Big Trouser. #4119. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4118. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4117. Path to Nowhere tier list - All characters ranked

Updated on November 2nd, 2026 - Version: 1.9.54

Path to Nowhere has a considerable variety of characters you can unlock. But if you are a beginner, finding out what hero to use can be problematic. Luckily, experts across the web have created a tier list for Path to Nowhere to solve this problem.

We have similar articles like this Neural Cloud tier list and Summoners War: Chronicles tier list, where we have also ranked all of the characters by their power and abilities from the best to worst. If you're playing different mobile games, try to search around - our website is brimming with tier lists and various guides for the most popular games. WHAT IS THE PATH TO NOWHERE TIER LIST?

This Path to Nowhere tier list is similar to the ones we have for other video games. There are four tiers: S, A, B, and C. Continue reading, and you will learn more about every tier.

Most players consider Demon to be the most overpowered hero in the game. His special attack stacks a shield for him and his allies. The more health points Demon has, the more powerful protection he will create.

He also has potent attack stats, allowing him to kill enemies fast.

Nox is the most accessible hero in Tier S. She can be unlocked by completing the 14-day event. Nox has incredibly high DPS and a passive ability that decreases your enemies’ defence. Moreover, Nox increases attack points upon killing enemies, which is one of the best abilities in Path to Nowhere. So, make sure to obtain this hero as soon as you can.

Labyrinth is the only hero in Tier S that has a B rarity. So, you can unlock her even if you don't play the game daily. Labyrinth is a damage dealer who takes the primary role in a team. She can break enemies’ shields and even destroy Demon’s shield.

Even though Baiyi has less DPS than Nox, she still can deal a lot of damage in a short period. Moreover, her skill significantly increases critical rate boost. She is also one of the fastest heroes in Path to Nowhere.

Langley is a top-level hero because of her particular skill. It provides you with an AoE attack that can hit a 3x3 area. So, Langley is a perfect option if you want to fight against bosses or groups of enemies.

Eirene is a magical attacker that probably has one of the best passive abilities in the game. While using an auto-attack, she creates a black hole that hits a 3x3 area. The only disadvantage is that Eirene is weak in melee fights.

Hamel is the only healer in Path to Nowhere that is worth being in Tier S. She has an AoE healing effect that helps keep your team's HP topped up in battle.

Countless Chelsea is one of the most complex heroes in Path to Nowhere. But in good hands, she brings excellent results. Countless Chelsea can summon a panther that can be used as a shield. Also, she has damage reduction, allowing her to take a lot of punishment and still survive.

The main feature of Demolia is her health points. She can quickly increase them and, after that, heal herself, which significantly increases her survivability. The only reason why she's not in Tier S is that there is a limit on her HP boost and healing.

Even though Serpent looks cute, she is one of the deadliest heroes in Path to Nowhere. While using a standard attack, she applies a slowdown effect to enemies and increases her speed. Moreover, when there are no enemies near Serpent, she will raise her attack.

RouLecca has poor DPS and can only deal damage using critical attacks, but she can increase her crit rate and damage while attacking.

Zoya is the Tier A hero most likely to appear in Tier S in the future. She has a 3x3 AoE attack that can deal significant damage. Zoya also has a lot of health points and has no problem killing enemies in short range. But the best thing about Zoya is her passive skill. It increases her attacking speed, making her suitable even in the later stages of the game.

Pricilla can summon a clone who helps her during battle. Additionally, she has high DPS, allowing you to kill enemies quickly. Unfortunately, her lack of health points doesn't make her worthy of becoming Tier S.

Hecate's ability has long range and hits every target in this range, which is extremely powerful. But Hecate doesn't have good survivability, so you should be careful while using her.

Aerial is the only healer in Tier A. The only difference between her and Hamel is that she is universal. Aerial has increased damage, which enables her to fight against enemies. And for increased damage, she gives up her healing capabilities. So, Aerial can't heal as effectively as Hamel.

Victoria is a hero with really significant damage. However, she forgoes health points for such a high attack capability. She will lower her health points to gain more attacks and kill enemies more effectively.

Luvia Ray is the most classic damage dealer in Path to Nowhere. She has high stats and a passive skill oriented toward increasing attack. Overall, she is a mighty hero who will always bring benefit to your team.

Crache has one of the best special attacks in the game. The AoE can deal a high amount of damage quickly. Moreover, this attack has an unblocking effect, so that opponents can't dodge it. The only disadvantage of Crache is that she has purely physical stats. Therefore, she must be complemented by powerful characters who can deal a lot of damage.

The best thing about EMP is that this hero is free. You can obtain her by completing the first chapter of the story. As for battle, she is perfectly suitable for the role of a background hero. Her special attack can wipe out low HP heroes and provide additional buffs for your team.

Tier B includes the following characters:

You can find out more about the most powerful heroes from Tier B below.

Cinnabar is a unique combination of powerful abilities in one character. She can create a 3x3 range shield protecting allies. Even though this shield doesn't have many health points, using it can still be handy during battles. Overall, Cinnabar is pretty powerful. She has a strong multiplier, allowing her to win battles easily.

Ninety-Nine is one of the best tanks in Path to Nowhere. You can exchange her health points in order to deal damage to enemies. On top of that, her extraordinary ability will reduce her health to get a significant attack bonus.

Sumire hits four times in a row in the same direction with her Special Ability. This special is extremely powerful on small maps, making Sumire more effective there. Also, she increases her damage when someone is opposite to her. Moreover, there are no limitations on increasing damage.

Even though Wolverine can't play the central role in the team, his slowing-down effect allows him to be effective even with higher-tier characters. Wolverine has special traps that stun enemies. These traps have a high range, making this hero super helpful.

Tier C includes characters that aren't recommended to use, even if you are a beginner.

The main feature of Pepper is her powerful attack speed. She can even increase it using a particular skill. But the main problem with Pepper is that she has no other stats to boast about.

There is nothing special about Gekkabijin. She has no powerful stats like the Tier S characters. Her unique ability provides her with additional attack and shield, but it isn't good enough to be competitive nowadays.

Even though the game has different characters with distinct abilities, it's best to only use the ones at the top of our Path to Nowhere tier list if you can - Tier S and Tier A - since they consistently perform the best.

Thank you for reading this guide - hope you find it helpful! And while you are here, make sure to read our Path to Nowhere beginner's guide as well.

#4116. Lego And TT Games Seemingly Tease A New Lego James Bond Game

The Lego games have been a part of many gamers' childhoods, but TT Games has more than proven in recent years that their family-friendly gaming adaptations can be enjoyed by just about anyone regardless of their age. While rumors have been circulating about what the next Lego gaming project would be after it was leaked to be a Warner Bros. property, some recent teases have fans thinking otherwise.

While it's far from an official confirmation of any kind, both TT Games and Lego themselves chiming in on the topic already has fans fully convinced that a previously cancelled Lego game could be getting the modern-day return it desperately deserves.

First spotted by CrazyLegoMoment on X, a suspicious series of tweets was made after it was announced Robert Pattinson would be taking the mantle of James Bond moving forward, starting with TT Games responding with a pair of eyes emoji when Shai Matheson (voice of Batman in Lego Batman: Legacy of The Dark Knight) joked that he would be "the next Lego Bond".

As if that wasn't enough, even the official Lego account responded by saying "he's got a license to build" when another fan posted about wanting an official Lego James Bond game made by TT Games.

Legacy of the Dark Knight has clocked up impressive enough review scores to make it the highest-rated Lego game ever.

While these could certainly just be some members of the studios trying to join in on the viral sensation and memes coming out of the news, an official announcement wouldn't be much of a surprise considering TT Games had already pitched several James Bond-themed Lego games in the past, one of which saw its entire pitch trailer leaked last year to the excitement of countless fans.

Having supposedly rejected TT Games' take on Bond for the subject material being "too mature" for the Lego in the past, the company has since branched out to countless adult franchises for official sets and even triple-A games like Legacy of The Dark Knight that Bond would feel right at home with for a full-blown adaptation.

Combined with the unique gameplay mechanics, open-world, and sheer level of detail offered by TT Games' previous Legacy of the Dark Knight and Skywalker Saga, a standalone Lego James Bond game would be a perfect fit with countless vehicles, gadgets, and costumes to experiment with.

With 27 films over the past 60 years to pull from, a Lego James Bond game isn't exactly starved for potential when it comes to levels and characters either, which would also offer the perfect tie-in game for whenever Robert Pattinson's upcoming Bond film releases.

What makes a franchise adaptation successful for you? And who do you think will win in a popularity contest: Dadish, Zayne, or GingerBrave? We dive into all things Warhammer Survivors in this week's (New and Improved!) Pocket Gamer Podcast, with a healthy dose of speculation on the community-nominated characters from the Pocket Gamer Awards in the mix.

The results for the nominations phase are in, and for Best Mobile Game Character, I'm surprised to see Zayne in there as opposed to Valko from Love and Deepspace! It's a pleasant surprise, of course, as I've always liked Zayne, while Iwan shares his thoughts on controversies and white bread.

Will believes that Dadish deserves the top spot, and it's up to you, the community, to pick your winners as voting is now open until the end of the year. Hopefully, you'll get to see your faves win at the awards show in London in January!

That said, we move on from the nomms onto Warhammer Survivors, which is the hot topic for the three of us in particular this week - and that's because we are all playing on different platforms, coming from different perspectives, and have mixed opinions on the Survivors-like.

For me, as a newbie to the franchise, the Warhammer coat of paint isn't really relevant to me, but even so, I had a blast playing through the roguelike as it is. I love the challenge and the replayability, as well as the lovely little surprises you get to unlock along the way. Iwan, on the other hand, feels like while it's a worthy entry into the genre, it lacks that extra spark that made the original Vampire Survivors so great.

Will is a bit of both - he thinks it's not the perfect game, but it's got enough going for it that makes it charming in its own way, especially for a Warhammer fan. With the roadmap for the roguelike having just been revealed, here's hoping we'll get to see more updates for it to make it shine like it should in the next few weeks!

#4114. GTA 6: How to Clone Keys

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

This wouldn’t be a Grand Theft Auto game without a little bit of … well, Grand Theft Auto. One of the first things you will likely be encouraged to do in Grand Theft Auto 6 is steal a car, and for the most part, it can be relatively easy to do. Break a window and hotwire it. Nothing more to it. Unfortunately, later in the game, especially in higher end neighborhoods, there will be vehicles with electric locks that require a bit of finesse to ensure the alarm doesn’t go off.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

At the beginning of the game, Jason will only have the ability to smash open a window to unlock the car’s door. This is something that has been apart of the series since its creation. In chapter 2, Lucia will learn how to Slim Jim a car to ensure that the alarm system won’t go off and you’ll have a cleaner getaway.

Unfortunately, some of the later cars won’t give you this option because they are keyless. This is what a key cloner is for. This will allow you to essentially hack into a car’s system and not only open the door but hotwire it in the process.

Unfortunately, early in the story you won’t be able to clone keys. You will have your trusty elbow and Slim Jim for the first two chapters, but once you hit Chapter 3, things change a little bit.

You will meet a man by the name of Randy. He is a car dealer who deals in hot cars (stolen) and has employed both Lucia and Jason to get him some of the fastest and most expensive cars possible. Don’t worry about smashing them up; so long as they can pull into his garage, he can fix it.

You will get a mission from Randy where he will want a Zorrusso located all the way Vice Beach (east). Head down and start this mission and Randy will call you to explain the situation.

By starting this mission, you will unlock the key cloner app on your phone, allowing you to finally be able to unlock some of the higher-grade vehicles. Be cautious, though, as cars that require a key cloner generally come with at least a standard tracker, which can alert police to your location if you’re not driving fast enough.

Regardless, after completing this mission, the car world is your oyster. Go out and have some fun.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4113. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4112. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game Ever

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's second remake of the original N64 game that first launched way back in 1998, is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published game on the Switch 2 ever. That accolade comes after the game sold more than 5.2 million copies in just four days following its November 5 launch last week.

This remake is already the Switch 2's second-best-selling Nintendo game at 5.2 million units sold, behind Mario Kart World's impressive 16.48 million copies sold to date. If The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time keeps this pace up, it could one day overtake Mario Kart World, though the Mario Kart series typically holds onto that top spot. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is still far and away the best-selling game on Switch.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the crown jewel of Nintendo's 40th Zelda series anniversary celebration, which also includes other games, products, and even an upcoming worldwide orchestral tour. Plus, a live-action Legend of Zelda film will debut in theaters worldwide on April 30, 2027.

Game Informer gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a 9.25 out of 10 in its review, with our reviewer Kyle Hilliard writing, "For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve the original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn't expect to be so moved."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched last week exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

For more, read this interview with the remake's producers about changes to the original game, easter eggs, the Bombchu bowling alley operator, and more, then check out this feature breaking down the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time easter eggs that did and didn't make it into this 2026 remake. After that, read about how the Switch 2 Pro controller can make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time even better, then check out this interview with award-winning composer and musician Jon Batiste about the Ocarina of Time score.

Pokémon Masters EX, the officially licensed game by DeNA, has brought tons of new Sync Pairs for players to collect and use with their fifth anniversary. This Pokémon Masters EX tier list is here to serve as a curated list of Sync Pairs that can help you in your journey of becoming the best Pokémon trainer.

You will find all the answers in this tier list as to whether a certain Sync Pair is better or worse than another. Keep in mind that tier lists are inherently subjective in nature.
